issues.item: Triggers: Sexual Trauma Cues: Comments on sexual violence
issues.explanation: 'Comments on sexual violence' is hard to reconcile with a primary trauma of life-threatening accident in the absence of any sexual-trauma content elsewhere in triggers, memory, threat, or appraisals. This is not just unusual; it suggests a different trauma theme than the stated index event.

issues.item: Maladaptive Strategies: Prevention Rumination: I dwell on how the event could have been prevented
issues.explanation: 'I dwell on how the event could have been prevented' can occur after accidents, but here the rest of the profile centers on sensory trauma cues and intrusive memory/avoidance rather than a coherent prevention-focused appraisal pattern. With Negative Appraisals absent and no threat/appraisal content linking to preventability, this strategy feels weakly grounded relative to the formulation and selected items.

vignette: Carlos, a 62-year-old Latin American surgeon, has experienced significant distress since a life-threatening accident in which he was involved in a severe car crash. The event left him with deep emotional scars that have affected his daily life and work. On the day of the accident, Carlos was driving home from the hospital after completing an emergency surgery late into the night. As he navigated through the rain-soaked streets, another vehicle lost control on a slippery curve and crashed directly into his car. The impact was violent and sudden, leaving Carlos dazed and struggling to escape the wreckage as the other car’s engine ignited in flames. Since then, known people who were related to the event—emergency responders and fellow surgeons who witnessed the aftermath of the crash—trigger intense distress for him. Even a specific texture associated with the accident—a gritty, charred material that clung to his clothing post-crash—becomes unbearable when he encounters it in various contexts. The vividness and realness of his memories are overwhelming; they intrude unbidden, leaving Carlos feeling as though he is reliving the event. He often finds himself pushing these intrusive thoughts away before fully processing them, only for them to return with renewed intensity later. These memories, more real than any ordinary recollection, contribute significantly to his distress. In response to this overwhelming memory and triggers, Carlos has adopted several maladaptive strategies that have gradually altered his daily life. He avoids situations that put physical stress on his body, such as running or even strenuous work in the hospital operating room. His avoidance extends beyond just physical stress; he gives up pleasant activities that once brought him joy, like playing soccer with friends and attending family gatherings. The thought of encountering a trigger during these events is too daunting to bear. One specific incident highlighted the extent of his avoidance behavior. During a routine check-up at a local clinic, Carlos encountered a doctor who had been present at the scene of the accident. This encounter triggered an intense panic attack, leading him to abruptly leave without completing the appointment. Since then, he has refrained from visiting that clinic and even avoids driving through the neighborhood where it is located. Carlos’s avoidance behaviors also extend to his professional life as a surgeon. He has become increasingly reluctant to perform surgeries involving high-risk patients, fearing that another stressful incident might trigger a relapse of his trauma symptoms. This has strained his relationship with colleagues who rely on his expertise and have noticed his withdrawal from complex cases. The cycle of avoidance has only deepened his distress. When he does engage in activities or encounters triggers—like the specific texture associated with the accident—it exacerbates his anxiety, leading him to further avoid these situations. This self-reinforcing loop has made it increasingly difficult for Carlos to maintain a semblance of normalcy in his daily life. Despite the profound impact on his personal and professional life, what finally brought Carlos to seek help was a realization that he could no longer ignore the emotional toll this trauma had taken. He is most afraid of losing control and becoming incapacitated by his symptoms, yet he hopes for relief from these overwhelming experiences and the ability to regain some semblance of normalcy in his life. Carlos’s journey towards recovery begins with acknowledging the need for support and understanding that his fear-driven behaviors have become a part of his daily existence. He is eager to explore ways to manage his triggers and memories, hoping to regain control over his life and return to the fulfilling career he once enjoyed.
